title: Regression surgery and incident prioritization — biweekly triage
content:
Biweekly window: 2026-03-16 to 2026-03-29
Prepared by: Aisha N. Patel (Applied ML) — rapid triage notes and prioritization for the model onboarding pipeline.

Purpose
- Condensed, surgery-style triage for the top regressions discovered in the onboarding evals and promptset runs. Aim: identify 1–2 immediate mitigations (canary / prompt fixes / fallback routing) and 3 medium-term engineering tickets for the sprint.

Executive summary (tl;dr)
- We observed a 5.7 percentage point drop in instruction-following pass-rate on the cross-domain onboarding suite vs the previous stable baseline (model v1.2 -> candidate v1.3-rc).
- Hallucination indicator (named-entity hallucination score) up +48% on finance/legal promptsets.
- Latency SLO unaffected; inference p95 consistent with baseline (within 3%).
- Top failure archetypes: slot-dropping in multi-turn form-filling, toxic-response regression on casual chit-chat edgecases, and factual hallucination for low-resource domain prompts.

Failure breakdown (counts are aggregated across promptset runs for the window)
- Slot-dropping (multi-turn): 472 failures, severity: high (breaks downstream workflow). Prompts affected: account-transfer, kyc-verification flavorgroups.
- Named-entity hallucination (NEH): 310 failures, severity: high for finance/legal promptsets where hallucinated entities carry regulatory risk.
- Tone/regeneration mismatch (safety edge): 128 failures, severity: medium (often recoverable by filter).
- Response truncation / early-stop: 94 failures, severity: medium-low (mostly long-chain reasoning prompts).

Data slices with largest deltas vs baseline
- Finance & Legal promptset group: instruction-follow rate delta -14% (largest), NEH +48%.
- Internationalization (non-en promptset bucket): latency stable but correctness down -7% for zh/es prompts (tokenization mismatch suspected).
- Long-context summarization subset (>1024 tokens): coherence score -9 points.

Notable anonymized examples (for debugging)
- Prompt: "Summarize client's KYC: transactions show L1 -> L3."
  Model output (failure): inserts a fabricated company name and a nonexistent transaction ID. Root cause note: model tends to overcommit on sparse structured records when instruction context is short.

- Prompt: "How to transfer $5000 from account A to B?" (multi-turn)
  Model output (failure): omits the confirmation step, fails to ask required verification question (slot-drop). Repro rate: 62% on repeated runs with same seed.

Root-cause hypotheses (quick list)
- Candidate v1.3-rc introduces subtle alignment drift under constrained decoding temperature settings used by the onboarding harness.
- Tokenizer model mismatch on some multilingual prompt variants leading to truncated context for zh/es.
- New pretraining data mix increased exposure to creative completions that increase NE hallucination in regulated prompt contexts.

Immediate mitigations (surgical ops) — ship within 48–72 hours if validated
1) Canary rollback of routing policy: redirect finance/legal traffic for 10% of production onboarding traffic to v1.2 and run differential telemetry (owner: Marcus Liu, due: 2026-03-31).
2) Prompt guard: insert a short wrapper for high-risk promptsets that enforces entity-presence checks + explicit ask-for-confirmation for multi-turn flows (owner: Rita Gomez, due: 2026-03-31). Implementation: lightweight wrapper in onboarding harness; no model change.
3) Automatic NE filter: post-process outputs for finance/legal to flag inserted named entities not present in input/context (owner: Jonah Kim, due: 2026-04-01). This is temporary until model fix.

Medium-term engineering work (sprint scope)
- Ticket ML-615: Add temperature sweep & decoding profile analysis to onboarding CI (owner: Aisha, estimate: 2s). Purpose: reproduce alignment drift under different decoding params. Linked: JIRA-AI-4821.
- Ticket INF-339: Tokenizer parity tests and small-batch e2e for zh/es inputs (owner: Marcus Liu, estimate: 3s).
- Ticket SAF-271: Create a targeted safety eval for low-frequency hallucination patterns derived from finance/legal prompt cluster (owner: Rita Gomez, estimate: 3s).

Operational monitoring updates
- Add a new per-promptset histogram for named-entity hallucination (daily), with alert if NEH > 20% for any high-risk tag. Owner: SRE observability (onboard with Redwood Console team).
- Track canary differential metrics for both instruction-follow rate and NEH ratio; alert threshold: 5-point drop or 30% relative NEH increase.

Promptset housekeeping (quick wins)
- Remove 12 near-duplicate prompts in the finance promptset that were amplifying the failure; consolidate into canonical prompts.
- Add 40 adversarial variants for multi-turn slot-testing (small script added to promptset generator; PR draft ready).

Risk & rollback plan
- If canary shows >8 point drop in instruction-follow for v1.3 across any one high-risk promptset at 10% traffic, abort rollout and revert routing to v1.2 for that tenant.
- If NEH persists despite wrapper+filter, escalate to hold and open model-swap rollback.

Open questions for next triage meeting
- Do we accept a temporary post-processing filter on production (compliance risk, false positives)? Security to weigh in.
- Is the tokenizer parity issue limited to the new tokenization config used in v1.3-rc or does it surface for older versions too?
- Should we expand the regression harness to include automated back-translation checks for non-en prompts?

Meeting agenda (next sync: 2026-03-31)
- 10 min: Quick metric walk (Aisha)
- 15 min: Canary plan review and gating (Marcus + SRE)
- 15 min: Prompt wrapper design & implementation plan (Rita)
- 10 min: Safety eval and NE filter tradeoffs (Jonah + Safety)
- 10 min: Decide go/no-go for wider rollout or hold.

Appendix: quick telemetry table (aggregated)
- instruction-follow baseline (v1.2): 87.9%
- instruction-follow candidate (v1.3-rc): 82.2%
- NE hallucination baseline (finance): 6.8%
- NE hallucination candidate (finance): 10.1%
- p95 latency baseline: 254 ms
- p95 latency candidate: 262 ms

Notes to reviewers
- This doc is intentionally surgical and action-oriented. Please add quick comments inline in the doc or tag owners in the JIRA tickets. We want canary decisions by EOD 2026-03-31.

Attachments / quick links (in-line)
- Diff dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/regression/diff-2026-03-16_03-29
- Canary playbook draft: github.com/redwood-inference/canary-playbooks/blob/main/finance-canary.md
- Promptset generator PR (draft): github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-gen/PR-27

---
Working notes (rough) — keep below for context:
- Repro runs for slot-drop have higher flakiness under sampling temperature 0.7; deterministic greedy reduces but doesn't eliminate.
- Early filter idea: if output contains a named entity not in input AND confidence(low) then redact + ask confirmation. Implementation unknown for confidence signal.
- Quick test: running the candidate with constrained beam-size (3) reduced some hallucinations in local tests but increased repetition on long-form summarization.

End of doc.
